subject: Pen test sampling, evidence transfer & retest eligibility for SOC 2 submission
messages:
From: Acme Compliance <acme-corp-compliance@acme.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: secops@blueshieldsec.com
Date: 2026-08-20T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Clarify penetration test sampling & evidence handoff for SOC 2

Hi Priyom,

We're preparing our SOC 2 Type II submission and need to include your most recent penetration test materials as supporting evidence. We received the 2025 PT report (thank you), but the auditor has two open questions:

1) Sampling: the auditor needs confirmation of the sampling approach used (how systems were selected, sample size, and whether any in-scope assets were excluded).
2) Evidence handoff: they asked for custody/transfer details for raw workpapers and whether we can obtain redacted test artifacts (exploit traces, screenshots) under an NDA.

Also, please confirm whether Redwood would consider a limited retest or targeted validation for vulnerabilities that were remediated after the report date, and whether you can provide a signed attestation that the scope and methodology align with industry standards (OWASP/OSSTMM or equivalent).

Can you confirm next steps and timeline? Our deadline for the auditor to receive evidence is 2026-09-10.

Thanks,
Caroline Mills
Senior Compliance Manager
Acme Corporation
attachments: Acme-PT-Report-2025.pdf

From: priyom_das@redwood.com
To: Acme Compliance <acme-corp-compliance@acme.com>
Cc: secops@blueshieldsec.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, mina_haddad@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-21T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify penetration test sampling & evidence handoff for SOC 2

Hi Caroline — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Rishi and Mina from our security programs team to confirm technical detail and sign-off. Quick answers up-front:

- Sampling: the pen test engaged scope (as in the report) was a risk-based sample of external infra and customer-facing services. We used a combination of threat modeling and production traffic volume to prioritize hosts; I'll ask Mina to pull the sampling matrix and selection criteria.
- Evidence handoff: we can provide redacted workpapers under NDA and a documented chain-of-custody CSV for the artifacts. Full raw exploit traces contain customer-sensitive data so we require redaction; BlueShield (our vendor) can produce sanitized traces.
- Retest: our standard is to allow targeted validation for high/critical CVEs if remediation evidence is available and the vendor (BlueShield) can rerun the specific verification.

I will follow up with a short timeline and the sampling matrix attached.

Best,
Priyom Das
Security & Trust Operations
Redwood Inference

Date: 2026-08-24T14:16:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Clarify penetration test sampling & evidence handoff for SOC 2

Hi Caroline, Priyom — thanks, I pulled the details from the engagement. Summary: 

- Methodology and standards: BlueShield conducted the engagement per a hybrid methodology based on OWASP Testing Guide for web components and NIST SP 800-115 techniques for network assessments; we document test cases and acceptance criteria in the workpapers.
- Sampling matrix: attached is an anonymized sampling_matrix.xlsx that maps service tiers, traffic percentiles, and selection rationale. We selected 12 hosts/systems for deep testing across 3 service groups (customer-api, auth, assets).
- Evidence artifacts: we can provide sanitized exploit traces and screenshots. Raw logs contain PII/tenant data; we will redact at the field level and provide a chain-of-custody.csv that records file creation timestamps and who handled the artifacts.
- Firm credentials: BlueShield is a CREST-aligned firm with public references; we can include their engagement letter and tester rosters on request.

On retests: our policy is to allow a focused verification of remediations for CVSS >=7 within 90 days of the initial report at no additional charge to the customer; after 90 days we offer a paid targeted validation. For acceptance by auditors, we can provide a signed attestation confirming the patch validation steps and date of verification.

Timeline: I can produce the sanitized artifacts and sampling matrix by EOD 2026-08-27, and a signed scoped attestation by 2026-08-30.

Attachments: sampling_matrix.xlsx (stub)

Regards,
Mina Haddad
Director, Security Programs
Redwood Inference

Caroline / Priyom / Mina — quick operational notes from remediation tracking: 

- Remediation status: of the 23 findings in the 2025 report, 18 are marked remediated in our internal tracker; 5 low-severity items are deferred (documented with compensating controls). We will provide the remediation evidence bundle (diffs, patch IDs, Jira links) as part of the artifacts.
- Retest eligibility: the 18 remediated items were verified internally; BlueShield ran targeted verification on 10 of these during the engagement close. For auditor acceptance, we recommend the focused retest for the top 6 high/critical fixes — we'll ask BlueShield to re-run and produce verification logs.
- Logistics for handoff: we propose a two-stage delivery: (1) sanitized workpapers and sampling_matrix.xlsx to your secure Drive folder (link requested) and (2) a DocuSign for the scoped attestation so you have a signed artifact. Attachments will be uploaded to a Redacted Evidence drive folder; access will be time-limited and logged.

Action items I can own: coordinate BlueShield for the focused verification (target completion 2026-09-06), produce remediation bundle (2026-09-02), and send DocuSign envelope for attestation (today).

- Rishi Malhotra
Head of Product Security
Redwood Inference
